searchText: related point, why not apply correlated penalties at `EPOCHS_PER_SLASHINGS_VECTOR` instead of `EPOCHS_PER_SLASHINGS_VECTOR // 2`? > Why is the balance of a slashed validator decreased immediately on slash_validator()? What invariant security property would be lost if the balance was only reduced on process_slashings() why not? its easier to just do it in place, rather than defer after spot checking a few things, it doesn't seem like it would impact anything to batch this one balance change at epoch boundaries so if that's equal from an effects perspective, i'd elect to smooth as much work out as possible over the epoch, rather than batch everything every SLOTS_PER_EPOCH > Why is a slashed validator not allowed to withdraw until EPOCHS_PER_SLASHINGS_VECTOR if correlated penalties (process_slashings) are applied on EPOCHS_PER_SLASHINGS_VECTOR // 2? they probably could other than the fact that the current design has additional disincentives against slashing we may as well keep -- 1) opp cost of locked stake, 2) additional inactivity penalties > why not apply correlated penalties at EPOCHS_PER_SLASHINGS_VECTOR instead of EPOCHS_PER_SLASHINGS_VECTOR // 2? the `// 2` factor means you sample from the middle of the rolling window of all slashings, and use this value to tally the cumulative slashings if you waited until the full length of the window, there could be stuff ahead of you that you should be penalized for that you otherwise would not In the spirit of correlating penalties of other network participants future actions should weight equally to past actions. If some event causes a mass slashing equally spaced over `EPOCHS_PER_SLASHINGS_VECTOR // 2`, the first affected will be penalized much less than that last

excerpts.author: dapplion
excerpts.content: related point, why not apply correlated penalties at `EPOCHS_PER_SLASHINGS_VECTOR` instead of `EPOCHS_PER_SLASHINGS_VECTOR // 2`?

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content:
> Why is the balance of a slashed validator decreased immediately on slash_validator()? What invariant security property would be lost if the balance was only reduced on process_slashings()
why not? its easier to just do it in place, rather than defer

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: after spot checking a few things, it doesn't seem like it would impact anything to batch this one balance change at epoch boundaries

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: so if that's equal from an effects perspective, i'd elect to smooth as much work out as possible over the epoch, rather than batch everything every SLOTS_PER_EPOCH

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content:
> Why is a slashed validator not allowed to withdraw until EPOCHS_PER_SLASHINGS_VECTOR if correlated penalties (process_slashings) are applied on EPOCHS_PER_SLASHINGS_VECTOR // 2?
they probably could other than the fact that the current design has additional disincentives against slashing we may as well keep -- 1) opp cost of locked stake, 2) additional inactivity penalties

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content:
> why not apply correlated penalties at EPOCHS_PER_SLASHINGS_VECTOR instead of EPOCHS_PER_SLASHINGS_VECTOR // 2?
the `// 2` factor means you sample from the middle of the rolling window of all slashings, and use this value to tally the cumulative slashings

if you waited until the full length of the window, there could be stuff ahead of you that you should be penalized for that you otherwise would not

excerpts.author: dapplion
excerpts.content: In the spirit of correlating penalties of other network participants future actions should weight equally to past actions. If some event causes a mass slashing equally spaced over `EPOCHS_PER_SLASHINGS_VECTOR // 2`, the first affected will be penalized much less than that last
